profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's Northern Virginia data center footprint, mapped in Prince William County near the company's Bristow-area operations, with no street address on file in this registry's underlying mapping data. Google's own Virginia locations page, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within its Northern Virginia footprint, so this specific structure is not independently identified beyond its OSM-derived coordinate.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own Virginia data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the company established a Virginia presence in 2009, purchased Northern Virginia land in 2017, opened its first facility in 2019, expanded a second Loudoun County facility in 2021, and opened a third in Prince William County in 2023; in 2025 Google announced a $9 billion investment for 2025-2026 spanning existing Northern Virginia sites and a new Chesterfield County campus. Google reports $15.6 billion in Virginia economic activity and over 36,000 employee volunteer hours since 2010.

Northern Virginia's Data Center Alley corridor, of which this Prince William County building is part, hosts large single-tenant campuses for AWS and Meta and colocation operators including Digital Realty and Equinix, all separately tracked in this registry, though Google's own public materials describe its Virginia footprint in aggregate rather than naming individual buildings or per-building capacity figures.

Loudoun and Prince William counties sit at the center of what industry trackers call Data Center Alley, the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world by aggregate power draw, a status Loudoun County's own economic development office has cited in public materials for over a decade. Dominion Energy, the regional utility, has repeatedly flagged this corridor in integrated resource plan filings with the Virginia State Corporation Commission as the single largest driver of new electricity demand in its Virginia service territory, prompting new transmission and generation investment. Virginia's data center sales-and-use tax exemption, administered by the Virginia Economic Development Partnership and renewed by the General Assembly, has been a material factor in Google and other hyperscalers continuing to expand in the corridor rather than building only in lower-tax states, though Google has not disclosed how much exemption value this specific facility has claimed.

reading.body:
Google has mapped one building within its Northern Virginia footprint in Prince William County, near its Bristow-area operations, but Google does not publish a megawatt IT capacity figure for any individual facility within its Northern Virginia campus. The company opened its third Virginia data center in Prince William County in 2023 as part of a distributed footprint across Loudoun and Prince William counties, and announced in 2025 a $9 billion investment for 2025-2026 spanning existing Northern Virginia sites and a new Chesterfield County campus, though building-specific capacity and square footage remain unpublished. Without published IT load specifications, the contribution of this individual structure to Virginia's data center buildout cannot be quantified from operator disclosures.

Virginia ranks first globally by aggregate data center capacity, with 326 mapped facilities across the state, and only 23 of those publish megawatt figures totaling 1,375.4 MW. This Prince William County building is one of three Google announced within its Northern Virginia footprint but does not itself contribute to the 23 published figures, making it unresolvable by the metrics this registry tracks. The Loudoun and Prince William corridor collectively anchors what the industry calls Data Center Alley and has been identified by Dominion Energy, the regional utility, as the single largest driver of new electricity demand in its Virginia service territory in successive integrated resource plan filings with the state.

Google's Northern Virginia presence sits alongside large single-tenant campuses for AWS and Meta and regional colocation operators, all separately tracked in this registry. Dominion Energy has repeatedly flagged the Loudoun-Prince William corridor as requiring new transmission and generation investment to accommodate data center demand growth. Virginia's sales-and-use tax exemption for data center equipment, administered by the Virginia Economic Development Partnership, has been cited by regional officials as a material factor in hyperscaler site selection within the corridor.
